questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the self-introduction whose greeting matches a first meeting with a professor
questions.stem: A graduate student arrives for a first meeting with a professor he has never spoken to, and he gives his own name and explains why he is there. Which sentence is the introduction a speaker in that position would actually use, and why?

options.text: 老师您好，我叫林涛，是这学期新来的交换生。
嗨，我叫林涛，是新来的交换生！快坐快坐。
options.misconception: treats a professor as a peer, using 嗨 and the imperative 快坐快坐 where the relationship requires a respectful pronoun and a deferential offer

options.text: 你好嘛，林涛，新来的交换生，随便坐啊。
options.misconception: believes the modal particles 嘛 and 啊 and the command 随便坐 are neutral in tone, when all three mark speech among friends

options.text: 林涛，新来的交换生。你好，我叫张伟。
options.misconception: puts a bare fact about a new student in first position and offers a second name, so the greeting is never actually said to the person being greeted

questions.explanation: The greeting in Chinese is chosen from the relationship, not from the content. 老师 is an honorific used before a title or a surname for a teacher or professor, and 您好 is the respectful greeting built on 您, the form of you used towards elders, superiors and strangers in a position of authority. Putting those two together with 老师您好 opens the meeting in a register the professor will hear as correct. The other three each break a different rule. B uses 嗨, which is a greeting between equals, and then tells a professor to sit down twice in the imperative, which no student does to a teacher. C uses 嘛 and 啊, both of which are particle markers of an easy, familiar tone, and 随便坐 turns an offer into permission granted by a host. D is the failure of a learner who treats the greeting as decoration and starts with the information instead, so the professor is never addressed and the speaker ends by giving a second, wrong name.
questions.hint: Ask which pronoun the position demands, and whether any modal particle or imperative crept in.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: match a greeting to the hour of the call and to the relationship
questions.stem: A student telephones a classmate at two in the afternoon to ask about a homework set, and she wants the opening to fit both the hour and the fact that she is interrupting something. Which opening does that job?

options.text: 下午好，打扰一下，我想问一下今天的作业。
早上好，打扰一下，我想问一下今天的作业。
options.misconception: assumes a general hello will do at any hour, when the three time-of-day greetings are tied to named parts of the day and one of them names the wrong part

options.text: 晚上好，我想问问作业，你现在方便讲十分钟吗？
options.misconception: reads 晚上好 as the courteous default rather than a greeting whose use is fixed to the hours after dark

options.text: 你好呀，我在楼下呢，你下来一趟呗。
options.misconception: assumes 你好呀 and the modal particle 呗 are register-neutral, when both are markers of casual speech between people of the same age

questions.explanation: Chinese has three time-of-day greetings and each covers a named stretch of the day: 早上好 is for the morning, 下午好 for the afternoon, and 晚上好 for the evening and the hours after dark. A call placed at two in the afternoon is named by 下午好 and not by either of the other two, so a speaker who reaches for 早上好 has not been impolite, they have been unintelligible about when they are speaking. The second half of the sentence matters as much. 打扰一下 is the fixed phrase used to announce that the speaker is interrupting someone and to apologise for the interruption in the same breath, and it is the reason the call can open with a request at all. C is the trap that sounds most careful: it does ask whether the other person is free, but it opens by naming the wrong hour, and the request for ten minutes at the end of the sentence does not repair an opening the other person found confusing. D is not a phone opening at all but a message to someone in the same building, and both 呀 and 呗 mark it as speech with a friend.
questions.hint: Ask what part of the day two in the afternoon falls in, and which phrase announces an interruption.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the farewell that suits a formal meeting ending with a professor
questions.stem: A research student has just finished a first meeting with a professor who introduced him to the whole department, and the two are standing up to leave the office together. Which farewell carries the weight the meeting deserves without a mismatch of tone?

options.text: 谢谢老师，我回去写封邮件向您请教细节，再见。
拜拜啦老师，改天我请客吃烧烤，我先走一步咯！
options.misconception: reaches for 拜拜, 啦, and 咯, all of which belong to a farewell between friends rather than to a departure from a professor's office

options.text: 老师我先撤了啊，回头聊，您有事微信喊我。
options.misconception: uses 我先撤了 and 回头聊 as though ending a conversation with an equal, and treats an obligation to a professor as a favour owed to a friend

options.text: 老师再见！拜拜！您也早点休息，明天见！
options.misconception: stacks a formal farewell on a casual one and then promises a meeting for tomorrow that nobody has agreed to, so the register and the commitment both fail

questions.explanation: 再见 is the neutral farewell and can be used with anyone; what changes with formality is the material placed around it. In the keyed sentence the three things that rise with formality are all present: 谢谢老师 names the thanks and the address, 写封邮件 is the written channel a student uses to approach a professor rather than a text message, and 请教 is the deferential verb for asking a teacher for guidance. The result is a farewell that closes a formal meeting properly. The other three fail in the same way, by dropping the register somewhere. B and C are entirely built from farewell vocabulary that peers use among themselves; 撤 and 聊 are short forms that a student does not use towards a professor, and 微信 as the default channel is a genuine statement about the relationship. D is the most instructive because it begins correctly, and then ruins itself by adding a second farewell in a lower register and a promise to meet again that the professor has not agreed to, which puts a demand inside the politeness.
questions.hint: Ask which words in each farewell would be out of place if the other person were an equal rather than a professor.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the question that asks for a surname and for the form of address in the right register
questions.stem: A visitor has been sent to the wrong floor and has to ask the receptionist at the desk for a name and for the form of address he should use, and he cannot begin by saying hey. Which question does both parts of the job in one sentence?

options.text: 请问您贵姓，我该怎么称呼您比较合适？
你叫什么名字，麻烦你大声一点报给我听。
options.misconception: softens an order with 麻烦 while keeping the second person pronoun 你 and a demand to speak louder, so the politeness cancels itself out

options.text: 你是谁呀，报上名来我才知道给你办。
options.misconception: treats the exchange as a confrontation, since 报上名来 is the phrasing of someone demanding a name rather than asking for one

options.text: 请问你叫什么名字呀，麻烦你告诉我一下。
options.misconception: believes 请 on its own makes a question respectful, when the pronoun still decides the register and a stranger at a desk is addressed with 您

questions.explanation: Two separate things are wanted here and Chinese has a word for each. 贵姓 is the honorific way to ask a stranger or a senior for a surname; it is not a stilted version of 你姓什么 but the correct form, and it exists precisely because the relationship is new. 称呼 then asks how the speaker should address that person, which is the question that actually solves the visitor's problem rather than merely recording a name. Notice that the pronoun is 您 throughout. B is a common learner sentence and it is instructive: 麻烦 does soften the request, but the sentence keeps 你 and adds a demand that the other person speak up, so the total effect is an order with an apology attached. C goes further and uses 报上名来, which belongs to a police officer or a parent, not to a visitor at an office desk. D is the subtlest and the most frequent error: the learner has correctly discovered 请 and 麻烦, has assembled a genuinely polite-sounding frame around them, and has left the pronoun at 你, so the politeness never reaches the person being addressed.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence contains a word for the honorific surname, a word for the form of address, and the respectful pronoun.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a request for a person's origin from requests for nationality or for a journey
questions.stem: Over coffee with a new client, a learner wants to ask where his colleague grew up and then whether she has settled in here. Which pair of questions asks for the origin in the standard form and stays polite?

options.text: 请问您是哪儿人？老家在哪儿？
你是哪的人？老家哪儿的？
options.misconception: fills the fixed pattern 哪儿人 with 哪 instead of 哪儿, which is a regional form rather than the standard one, and drops the respectful pronoun

options.text: 请问您是哪国的人？老家在哪儿？
options.misconception: reaches for 哪国 because it sounds careful, and so asks about nationality, a different category from the province or town a person comes from

options.text: 请问您是从哪儿来的呀，老家那边冷不冷？
options.misconception: asks which journey the person is on, and then assumes a northern climate from a person whose home has not been named

questions.explanation: 哪儿人 is the standard word for the place a person comes from, and it is a fixed shape: the question word 哪儿 plus the bound suffix 人. 老家 in the second question names the same place in a warmer register and is how a speaker asks after the town or village rather than the province, so the pair works as a natural two-step question. The distractors each represent a real attempt to be careful that turns out to change the question. B is the failure of a learner who treats 哪儿 as decoration and puts the bare 哪 in its place; the result is a regional form, understood in some places and not understood as standard anywhere, and the pronoun has gone as well. C is the confusion between 哪儿人 and 哪国人, which asks which country a person holds a passport of rather than where they are from, an error that can be awkward in exactly the polite situation it was meant to smooth. D is subtler: 从哪儿来的 does ask where someone came from, but in this context it points at the journey or the arrival rather than at the origin, and 冷不冷 then builds an assumption about a climate that nobody has mentioned.
questions.hint: Ask whether the question is about a place of origin, a nationality, or a journey, and check the word order 哪儿 plus 人.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the request that asks for a route rather than for a place or a number of buses
questions.stem: A visitor is standing at a street corner with a phone in his hand and has to reach the provincial museum before it closes. He does not want a map, he wants to be told how to go. Which opening asks for what he actually needs?

options.text: 请问去博物馆怎么走？走过去要多久？
请问去博物馆在哪儿？走过去要多久？
options.misconception: substitutes 在哪儿 for 怎么走, so the visitor is offered the address of the museum rather than the route he has to walk

options.text: 请问去博物馆怎么走？我自己看得懂地图的。
options.misconception: adds a declaration that he can read a map, which tells the speaker to stop helping and answers a question nobody asked

options.text: 请问去博物馆有多少路？我想坐几号线地铁。
options.misconception: treats 多少路 as a question about the number of routes or buses, when the speaker is on foot and the real question is which line to take

options.text: 请问去博物馆怎么走？走过去要大概多少时间？
options.misconception: keeps 怎么走 but then stacks two second clauses, and the longer question loses the deadline the visitor actually came with

questions.explanation: 怎么走 is the word that asks for a route. It is built on the verb 走, so the answer can contain the turns, the junctions and the number of minutes, and the whole exchange then has what it needs. Adding a second question about how long the walk takes is what a visitor with a closing time needs, and it is the reason the keyed sentence is the useful one. B is the most common error and it is a small substitution: 在哪儿 asks where the museum is, so the answer is an address or a landmark and the visitor still does not know which way to turn. C is a well-meant offer of independence that the speaker hears as a refusal, and the speaker has no reason to stop giving directions. D misunderstands 多少路, which counts routes or buses, and adds a question about a metro line when the speaker is on foot. E is not wrong so much as wasteful, and the lesson is worth drawing: 怎么走 plus 大概多少时间 says the same thing twice with more words, and in a hurried exchange the extra words are what a speaker ends up dropping anyway.
questions.hint: Ask which word carries the verb of travelling, and then whether the second question is one the visitor needs answered.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: construct a food order when the dish name is unknown
questions.stem: A diner cannot read the menu and wants to order by saying what is in the dish. Which sentence actually places an order with a waiter, using only ingredients as the description?

options.text: 我要一份用猪肉和白菜做的那个菜，麻烦你了。
猪肉加白菜的那个，给我一份就可以了。
options.misconception: describes the dish and names a measure word but supplies no ordering verb, so the waiter receives a description rather than a request

options.text: 我很喜欢吃猪肉和白菜，请给我看一下菜。
options.misconception: reads the same request as a complaint about the menu and answers a different question about the ingredients

options.text: 猪肉白菜多少钱一份？太贵我就要别的了。
options.misconception: turns the order into a question about price, which stops the waiter placing anything before the answer arrives

questions.explanation: A Chinese food order has three working parts: an ordering verb, the thing ordered, and a measure word with a number. The keyed sentence has all three, in order: 我要 is the ordering verb, 一份 is the number and measure word, and 用猪肉和白菜做的那个菜 is the description standing in for a name the diner does not have. Pointing at a dish by its ingredients is a normal thing to do in a restaurant, and the trailing 麻烦你了 keeps the request soft, since asking a waiter to identify something from a description is asking them to do work. B is the failure that looks closest to correct: it does supply 给我一份, and 一份 is the right measure word, but there is no verb that does the ordering, so what the waiter hears is a description with a quantity attached, and a hungry waiter will wait for the missing half. C is a well-formed sentence aimed at a different speech act, since 请给我看一下 is a request to see the menu, not to order. D leads with the price question, which in a real restaurant is answered before anything is placed, and the last clause then cancels the order it never made.
questions.hint: Ask which word does the ordering, which word counts the portions, and which part stands in for the name on the menu.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: identify which sentences are well-formed and correctly aimed requests
questions.stem: A traveller in a small tea shop needs to know what a pot costs and how much to buy. Four of the five sentences below are correctly formed requests that do what the traveller intends. Which four?

options.text: 这一壶茶多少钱？我先听个数再决定。
这一壶茶贵不贵？要是贵我就换一家。
这一壶茶水二两够吗？要是太多就换小壶。
这一壶茶一共多少钱？麻烦您写个单子给我。
这一壶茶一壶多少钱呀，老板您看着收就行。
options.misconception: repeats the measure word inside one noun phrase, so the question has no quantity left to ask about, and then withdraws the question by handing over the decision

questions.explanation: Four of these ask for something a shopper genuinely needs, and the difference between them is what they ask for. A asks for the number and nothing more, which is the plainest price question. B asks whether the price is high rather than what it is, which sounds weaker and is not, because a shopkeeper who hears 贵不贵 will usually volunteer the figure, and the sentence has also protected the speaker by making the next clause conditional. C asks about an amount, and 二两 is the weight the tea trade actually uses, so this is a question about quantity rather than about cost. D asks for the total and adds a receipt, which is a request to have the figure written down. E is wrong twice over. The measure word is repeated inside a single noun phrase, so 茶一壶一壶 is not a quantity a shopkeeper can read, and the closing clause then hands the price decision back to the seller, which means the traveller never learns what anything costs and has, in effect, agreed in advance to pay whatever is asked.
questions.hint: For each sentence, name the thing actually requested, and check that the measure word appears once in its noun phrase.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: match a named dish to the adjectives that describe its flavour
questions.stem: A menu lists a dish written in four characters, and a diner wants to know what the taste will be before ordering it. Which pair of adjectives best describes the dish named 麻婆豆腐 and the order in which the two tastes arrive?

options.text: 麻辣，豆腐很嫩，入口先是麻，然后是辣。
酸甜，豆腐外脆里嫩，上面浇的是糖醋汁。
options.misconception: confuses the dish with a sweet and sour one, where the two adjectives belong to a completely different family of dishes

options.text: 清淡，豆腐是清蒸的，上面只撒了一点葱花。
options.misconception: reads the four characters as a description of a steamed dish, when the name itself carries a hot and numbing flavour

options.text: 香甜，豆腐炖得很软，甜味全在汤里。
options.misconception: adds a sweetness that the name does not promise, and treats 麻 as an abbreviation for a seasoning rather than as the taste itself

questions.explanation: The name of a dish is allowed to tell you the taste. In 麻婆豆腐 the two taste characters are exactly the first two of the name: 麻 is the numbling tingle that Sichuan pepper gives, and 辣 is the heat of chilli, and a dish that carries both in its name is one a diner should be warned about in advance. The keyed answer adds the third fact worth knowing, which is the order, because the numbing arrives on the tongue first and the heat follows, and anyone who has not eaten it will be surprised by the first of the two. The distractors are not random flavours; each is a real category of dish, and the error is one of matching. B describes the sweet and sour family, which is a different kitchen altogether. C describes 清淡, the plain steamed and broth-based family, and reaches for it out of a learner's reasonable guess that a tofu dish must be gentle. D is the subtler trap, because it keeps the idea of a soft texture and a fragrant sauce, and then adds a sweetness the name never promised, treating 麻 as if it were a short form of a seasoning rather than as the taste itself.
questions.hint: Read the name and ask which two taste characters it starts with, and in which order they appear on the tongue.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: state a dietary restriction so that the host can act on it
questions.stem: A guest who cannot eat chilli is at a table where the host has just set down a Hunan dish and is offering to add more. Which sentence passes on the restriction in a form the host can actually act on?

options.text: 我不吃辣，这道菜麻烦您别放辣椒。
我不能吃辣椒，这道菜麻烦您别放辣椒。
options.misconception: uses 不能 instead of 不吃, so the host hears a physical inability rather than a matter of eating and may press the guest to try a little

options.text: 我是不吃辣的，您这道菜少放点辣椒就行了。
options.misconception: asks for the chilli to be reduced, which is not the same request as asking for none, and 就行了 then closes the negotiation before it opened

options.text: 我今天忌口，辣椒不能吃，您看着办就行。
options.misconception: names a general state of dietary avoidance without saying which ingredient is at issue, so the host has to guess which dish to adjust

questions.explanation: A restriction has to arrive as a fact plus an instruction, because the host cannot act on a mood. 不吃 states the fact, that this guest does not eat this thing, and 麻烦您别放辣椒 states the instruction, leave the chilli out of this particular dish. That is a complete message and it is the one the host needs. B is the error that sounds more careful and is less usable: 不能吃 says the guest is incapable rather than unwilling, which invites the very response the guest is trying to avoid, in which the host says a little cannot hurt. C is the commonest sentence of all and it quietly breaks the request. 少放点 asks for less instead of none, which is fine for seasoning and unacceptable for an allergy or a medical reason, and 就行了 then adds the pressure of a conversation being closed. D has the opposite problem to C: it signals that something matters without saying what, and 您看着办 hands the decision to a host who has no information to decide with, so the host will do nothing in particular and the guest will take a risk.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence gives the host a fact and an instruction, and whether the instruction is none or only less.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: restate a two-part directions instruction without changing either turn
questions.stem: A passer-by has given two instructions in a single breath. Which restatement keeps both of them, in the right order and with the same outcome, for a visitor who has to repeat them to a companion who was not listening?

options.text: 往前走，到第二个十字路口往左拐，拐过去就看见了。
往前走，到第二个十字路口往左转，转过去就看见了。
options.misconception: swaps 拐 for 转, which is accepted in speech but asks for a manoeuvre of a vehicle and loses the plain pedestrian sense of the instruction

options.text: 往前走，过了十字路口再往左拐，拐过去就看见了。
options.misconception: turns 第二个 into a single unspecified junction, so the companion is told to turn at a place the original speaker did not name

options.text: 往前走，到第二个十字路口往右拐，拐过去就看见了。
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the turn and keeps everything else, which is the change that sends the visitor to the wrong street

questions.explanation: A directions answer is a sequence with an ordinal in the middle of it, and the whole job of restating it is to move that sequence without disturbing anything. The keyed sentence keeps 往前走 first, keeps the ordinal 第二个, keeps 十字路口 as the landmark, keeps the turn as 往左拐, and keeps 拐过去就看见了 as the confirmation. B is the item that most readers will accept and the reason is worth explaining: 转 and 拐 are both used for a change of direction in modern speech, but 转 is originally the verb for a vehicle turning or a body rotating, while 拐 is the one that pictures a person leaving one road for another at a corner. The practical rule is that 拐 is the safer word for walking instructions, and the distractor is here because a learner who hears 转 and writes 拐 has not lost the meaning. C loses the count, which is the one piece of information the companion needs most. D is the change that actually matters, and it is the reason an item like this is worth a question at all: nothing in the sentence signals an error to a listener who has not seen the street.
questions.hint: List the four elements of the instruction in order, then check each one against what was said.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: report that instructions were received without telling the speaker to stop
questions.stem: A visitor has just been given directions and understands most of them. He wants the other person to know the instructions landed, and he does not want to sound as though he is dismissing them. Which sentence reports that without dismissal?

options.text: 明白了，谢谢您，我记下来了。
我知道了，行了，不用再说了。
options.misconception: joins 我知道了 to 行了 and 不用再说了, which together tell the speaker that their help is finished and unwelcome

options.text: 嗯，我大概明白了，别的先不管。
options.misconception: hedge the confirmation and then narrow the conversation, so the speaker learns that the instructions were not really followed

options.text: 好的好的，知道了知道了，懂了懂了。
options.misconception: repeats the same confirmation three times, which in Chinese is how a listener signals that the talk is going too slowly, not that it was received well

questions.explanation: Chinese has more than one way to report reception, and they are not interchangeable. 明白了 states that the content has arrived and has been understood, and in the keyed sentence it is followed by the two things a speaker should add: thanks, and a statement that the information is being kept, since a stranger who has given directions is owed that much. B is the trap because 我知道了 is not wrong in itself. What breaks it is the pair that follows. 行了 ends a matter and 不用再说了 tells the other person to stop talking, so the sentence is not a confirmation at all but a dismissal with a confirmation in front of it. C begins with 嗯, which is the sound of a listener who is not yet sure, and hedges with 大概 before immediately narrowing the conversation to something else, so the speaker hears that the directions were not retained. D is the item a learner meets most often in films and misunderstands most often in life. Repeating a confirmation is the Chinese sign for slow down, and three repetitions in a row is not enthusiasm but a request to end the conversation before it has finished.
questions.hint: Ask what the sentence would let the speaker infer about whether to go on helping.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: ask a speaker to repeat without complaining about how they speak
questions.stem: A learner has lost a street name in the middle of a stranger's directions and needs it again. Which sentence gets the name repeated while keeping the request inside a form the stranger will not resent?

options.text: 不好意思，麻烦您再说一遍，我没听清那两个字。
不好意思，您再说一次吧，我没听清，能大声点吗？
options.misconception: asks the stranger to change how loudly he speaks, which turns a request for information into a complaint about the speaker

options.text: 不好意思，您能不能不要说得这么快，我听不清。
options.misconception: also complains about the speaker, and 说得这么快 judges the pace rather than reporting on the listener's own hearing

options.text: 不好意思，你再说一遍吧，我刚才没听清那两字儿。
options.misconception: keeps the second person pronoun 你 throughout and drops the measure word, leaving 那两字儿 without the number word that a count requires

questions.explanation: A good request for a repeat does three things: it apologises for the interruption, it uses the polite set phrase 麻烦您, and it says exactly what was missed, so the speaker knows what to repeat. Naming 那两个字 tells the stranger that it was the name and not the second turn, which means the stranger repeats the right thing instead of the whole speech. B and C are the two natural ways a learner asks for a repeat and the two that cause offence, and the mechanism is the same in both: each comment is on the speaker rather than on the listener. 能大声点吗 asks for volume and 不要说得这么快 asks for a slower pace, and a person who has just given directions to a foreigner hears both as a judgement. D makes two separate slips. The pronoun drops from 您 to 你, which is a change of relationship rather than a typo, and 那两字儿 has lost the number word that the count needs, since a number and its measure word are a single unit in Chinese and one of them cannot stand alone.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence says what was missed, and whether any clause comments on the speaker rather than on the listener.

questions.learningObjective: correct a speaker's own error at once without blaming the listener

不是不是，应该是周一，不是周二。
options.misconception: uses the negative particle 不是 where a correcting 我是说 is needed, and so sounds like the speaker is now negating his own correction rather than replacing the first date

options.text: 你听错了，我刚才说的就是周二。
options.misconception: puts the error on the listener with 你听错了, and then repeats the corrected date as though nothing had gone wrong

options.text: 我刚才说的是周一，我刚才说的是周一，我刚才说的是周一。

questions.explanation: Chinese repairs a mistake by naming it and then supplying the substitute, and the phrase that does the naming is 我是说, which literally means what I meant was. It is the reflexive move: the speaker takes the error back, and 是说 points forward to the corrected material, so the rest of the sentence is unambiguous. B is the trap that looks like a stronger correction. 不是 is not a repair at all, it is the negative particle, and 不是不是 is the way a speaker contradicts somebody else; in a self-repair the listener is left unsure whether the speaker now believes the meeting is on Monday or on Tuesday. C is the version that damages a relationship, because 你听错了 declares that the fault lies in the other person's hearing, and the sentence then goes on to state the correct date with no acknowledgment that anything went wrong. D is worth dwelling on for a moment, because repetition is a real technique in Chinese and works for emphasis. It cannot work for repair, since the wrong information is what is being repeated and the right information never appears.

questions.learningObjective: interrupt in a group and correct a figure without insulting anyone

B is the version that turns a correction into a duel: 你听我说 is an imperative telling the other person to stop talking, and in front of two colleagues it is a public assertion about who has the right to speak. C is subtler and worth pausing on, because it is built from polite pieces. It apologises, it marks the interruption, and then it asks the group a question, which means the colleague who misstated the price is now being examined rather than quietly corrected. D is the failure of nerve that many learners default to, and it is the worst of the four outcomes for the listener, since the group stops and nobody has been told anything.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: concede a step while keeping the disagreement open
questions.stem: A learner has heard a colleague propose a plan he thinks is only partly workable, and the client he is sitting next to is not someone he wants to argue in front of. Explain in your own words how a speaker in this position concedes one step and still leaves room to disagree later, and say why the obvious alternatives are worse.

answer.exemplar: A concession of this kind has to be visibly temporary, and in Chinese the temporary is carried by three things at once: the adverb 先, the verb pattern that frames the step as an experiment rather than a decision, and a clause that promises a return. In the keyed sentence 好 concedes immediately, so the colleague is not left feeling he has won an argument, 先按这个试一次 frames what has just been agreed as one trial, and 不合适我们再调 puts the word we in the sentence so that the later change belongs to both of them. A learner who uses this and then says nothing about the plan again has not conceded provisionally, he has simply not objected yet, and the difference matters because the first sentence tells the client that the plan is still being examined while the second tells the client it has been accepted. The two obvious alternatives fail for opposite reasons, and it is the symmetry that makes them worth teaching. The flat agreement 那就按你的意思办吧 followed by 我不多说了 is worse because it closes the discussion explicitly, and closing a discussion in front of a third party is a stronger act than disagreeing quietly. The other alternative, repeated agreement, is worse because the client is a stranger to the argument and can hear repetition for what it is. Two of the real options here are marked as model sentences: one concedes and reopens, the other concedes and shuts. A speaker who knows both patterns can choose the one the situation needs, and that is the outcome the teaching should aim for.

questions.explanation: This item is marked as correct for treating the concession as something the speaker actively constructs, with 先, a trial framing, and a shared pronoun carrying the promise of a later return, and for explaining both tempting alternatives rather than only the bad one. The contrast between conceding and reopening and conceding and shutting is the teachable content here, because a learner can recite the first pattern and still fail to use the second when the client is the one who needs closing off.
questions.hint: Ask which word makes the agreement temporary, and what the speaker would still be able to say in ten minutes.

questions.learningObjective: correct a colleague's record without asserting that the colleague is wrong

options.misconception: opens with a second person accusation and then adds 根本, which removes any possibility of a second opinion being available

questions.learningObjective: refuse a request that has already been promised elsewhere
questions.stem: A colleague asks for two hours of help tomorrow, and the learner has already promised that time to somebody else. The answer has to be no, and the working relationship has to survive it. Which sentence does both?

options.text: 今天实在抽不开身，明天上午我一定帮你，行吗？
今天不行，我很忙，你找别人吧。
options.misconception: gives the reason and then hands the problem back in the same sentence, so the colleague is left to solve it unaided

options.text: 可以呀，不过我明天一早就要交稿，恐怕做不完。
options.misconception: says yes and withdraws in the following clause, which is worse than a plain no because the colleague has already begun to rely on the promise

options.text: 抱歉，最近事情太多了，我帮不了你这个忙。

C is the most common error in learner speech and the most damaging, because 可以呀 has already been heard as a promise and cannot be taken back; everything after the comma is a retraction delivered to someone who has started planning. D is a refusal with no alternative anywhere in it, and the 抱歉 is doing all the politeness work by itself.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence contains a reason, a limit, and an offer, and whether anything is said before the refusal.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: convert a vague wish to see someone into a proposal with a time
questions.stem: Stage one: a student needs fifteen minutes with a busy advisor and has written a message that gives no day and no time. Diagnose precisely what is wrong with it. Stage two: rewrite it as a request that proposes a specific slot and still leaves the advisor an easy way to refuse.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. Two things are wrong and they are different in kind, so they need different repairs. The message gives no day and no time, which means the advisor has to produce both before anything can be agreed, and that is work the student should be doing. The second fault is that the message ends by asking the advisor to decide when, which puts the whole scheduling problem on the person who is busiest. A learner who has fixed only the first fault has still written a message that costs the reader effort, so the diagnosis has to name the direction of the work as well as the missing information. Stage two. The repair is to supply a weekday and an hour, and then to lower what the request costs the reader. The keyed rewrite proposes a specific slot, and it adds a small piece of information that changes the psychology of the whole message: the student is already going to be there ten minutes early, which means the advisor can simply say no without arranging anything, and can say yes without having to fetch anybody. The result reads as a request rather than a summons, because the person who can decline cheaply is not under any pressure to be polite. An alternative rewrite that names only the day, or that apologises at length before naming the time, is weaker in two ways, and the learner should be able to say both: the first pushes the choice of hour back onto the advisor, and the second spends the reader's attention on the apology before the reason for reading appears.

questions.explanation: The pairing is deliberate: stage one is a diagnosis that has to distinguish a missing fact from a reversed burden, and stage two is a production task with a checkable result. Marking the exemplar correct for the diagnosis, the concrete slot, and the low-cost refusal the rewrite offers.
questions.hint: Ask what information the reader is being asked to supply, and what the request gives them in return for answering.

questions.stem: Four lines from a short written request to a landlord have been cut out of order. Only one sequence produces a letter that is read as a request. Which sequence is it?

options.text: 张先生您好： / 我下个月要出差三个月，租期还有半年。 / 想跟您商量一下，能不能把八月和九月两个月的房租减一些。 / 如果方便，本周五下午我去您那儿，当面把情况说清楚。

张先生您好： / 如果方便，本周五下午我去您那儿，当面把情况说清楚。 / 我下个月要出差三个月，租期还有半年。 / 想跟您商量一下，能不能把八月和九月两个月的房租减一些。
张先生您好： / 我下个月要出差三个月，租期还有半年。 / 如果方便，本周五下午我去您那儿，当面把情况说清楚。 / 想跟您商量一下，能不能把八月和九月两个月的房租减一些。

questions.explanation: A short written request in Chinese runs in the same order the conversation would, and the sequence that works is the one in the first option. The salutation comes first because the letter has to be addressed to somebody before it means anything. The facts come second, and they are facts rather than appeals: a period of absence and a term still running give the reader what he needs in order to decide anything. The request comes third, and it is a request, with 想 and 能不能 doing the work of making the ask a proposal the reader may decline. The closing line comes last, and it is the part learners leave out, because it converts a request into an appointment, which means the landlord arrives at Friday afternoon already knowing what is being proposed. The second option puts the request first, so the reader meets an ask before he has a reason for it. The third offers a time before there is anything to discuss, which is an imposition. The fourth is the commonest student order and the worst of the three, since it takes the reader all the way to a booked afternoon before the request finally appears.
questions.hint: Ask which line a reader needs before any other, and which line arrives too early in each wrong order.

啊，你就是接电话的人吧，我问你个事。

questions.learningObjective: compare the openings of an email and a formal letter to the same manager
questions.stem: A student must open a message to a manager twice: once as an email and once as a formal letter. Which statement about the two openings is accurate?

options.text: The email can open with 张经理您好 and the letter with 尊敬的张经理, and both openings are formal
The email can open with 亲爱的张经理 and the letter with 张经理您好, on the grounds that a warmer opening suits the shorter channel
options.misconception: reverses the two registers and reaches for 亲爱的, a warm form used with people one already knows, and lets a channel's length decide its register

options.text: The two openings have to be identical, because both documents are written and neither is speech
options.misconception: assumes writing is a single register, which is what produces a learner who opens every email like a clerk writing a letter

options.text: The email must open with 尊敬的张经理, the letter can open with 张经理您好, and the reason is that a letter is the shorter document

B gets the direction backwards and reaches for 亲爱的, which is a warm form used with people one already knows; the length of a channel does not decide its register. C is the belief that writing is a single register, and it produces a learner who opens every email with a line from a letter and sounds like a nineteenth-century clerk. It has more conventions than an email rather than fewer, and 尊敬的张经理 belongs to the paper letter and not to the message.
questions.hint: Ask which opening exists because of the paper convention and which one exists because there are no paper conventions to follow.

questions.learningObjective: give an authority a reason that is specific and pitched correctly
questions.stem: A student missed a lecture and has to tell the tutor why, and the tutor has a rule about unexcused absence. Which excuse is pitched for a tutor and gives the tutor something to weigh?

老师说"我昨天有事"，然后什么也不多说，等老师自己猜。
options.misconception: supplies no reason at all, so the tutor has nothing to weigh and the silence makes the omission look deliberate

options.text: 老师说"我错了，我以后一定不迟到，请您原谅我一次吧"，把原因完全省掉。
options.misconception: offers a promise and a plea in place of a reason, and a promise about the future is not evidence about the past

options.text: 老师说"我昨天发烧了，昨天真是不巧"，语气轻松得像在跟朋友聊天。
options.misconception: keeps a real reason but sets it in a light conversational tone, which undercuts the illness at the moment it is being reported

questions.explanation: An excuse given to somebody with authority has to do two things that are in tension: give a reason specific enough to be checked, and give it in a register that does not sound like an excuse. The keyed sentence manages both. 发烧了 with 吃了药在家休息 is a concrete, verifiable account, and a lecture is missed because a student is ill often enough that the account is plausible, which is what makes it worth telling. The apology comes after the reason rather than before it, and that order matters, because an apology first spends the tutor's attention on the speaker's feelings. The distractors each break one of the two requirements. B supplies neither, and the silence that follows a vague answer is the single most damaging thing a student can do, because it invites the tutor to fill in a worse reason. questions.learningObjective: choose the address form that fits a colleague who is an engineer

我们部门新来的同事是李老板，以后技术上的事找他就行。
options.misconception: uses 老板, which addresses an owner or a shopkeeper and misidentifies an engineer in front of a visitor

options.text: 我们部门新来的同事是李总，以后技术上的事找他就行。
options.misconception: uses 总, which marks a person in charge, so a new colleague with no reports is announced as a boss

options.text: 我们部门新来的同事是李先生，以后技术上的事找他就行。
options.misconception: uses the courtesy form for a man one does not know, which is a stranger's form and not the one a department uses about itself

The full word 工程师 is the job; 工 on its own is what colleagues and managers actually use to address and to refer to an engineer, so 李工 and 张工 are the everyday forms and they are respectful, which is the part that surprises learners. The four options here are all well-formed sentences, and the test is not grammar at all: it is whether the word describes the person in front of the other person. 老板 is for a proprietor or a shopkeeper. 总 is for whoever is in charge, and applying it to a newcomer with no reports makes the introduction describe a different organisation. 先生 is a courtesy form used towards a man one does not know, and it is the register of a hotel foyer, not of a department talking about itself. questions.hint: Ask which single character is used on its own to address an engineer, and what each of the other two titles would tell a stranger.

questions.learningObjective: place something relative to a landmark using a locative noun
questions.stem: A learner must say where a flat is, in a way a listener can picture, using the pattern that puts the place next to something else. Which sentence is right?

我家在旁边地铁站，走路五分钟就到超市了。
options.misconception: treats 旁边 as an adjective placed before the noun, when it is a locative noun that has to follow the thing it is next to

options.misconception: drops 站 from 地铁站, so 地铁 names the system and the speaker has given the listener a different place

options.text: 我住在旁边，走路五分钟就到超市了。
options.misconception: leaves the locative without a reference point, so the listener is told something is nearby without being told what it is near

questions.explanation: 旁边 and similar words are locative nouns, and a locative noun behaves in a particular way: it needs a reference point, and that reference point comes first. So the sequence is 地铁站 plus 旁边, with or without the linking 的, and both forms are standard. What does not work is putting the locative in front, because 旁边 is not an adjective and cannot modify a noun in that position, so 旁边地铁站 is not a place. The option that drops the locative's anchor is a different failure and is the commoner one in speech: 我住在旁边 is a perfectly ordinary sentence to say while standing in a corridor, and it is uninformative on a map. The remaining distractor is a word-level error rather than a structure error, and 地铁站 is two characters that learners frequently shorten to 地铁, which is a real word naming the system or the line rather than the station on the map. Worth telling learners that the diminutive ending on a locative, as in the third option, is not an error either: in the north a locative noun takes it routinely, and a regional form is a variety rather than a mistake.
questions.hint: Ask which word is the locative noun, what it has to follow, and what happens when its reference point is removed.

questions.learningObjective: describe a sequence of weather with intensifiers and change-of-state verbs
questions.stem: A learner wants to say that it was very cold in the morning, that rain started later, and that it cleared in the afternoon. Which sentence puts all three facts into natural Chinese?

options.text: 早上还冷得很，后来下起雨来了，下午又转晴了。
早上是很冷，后来是下了雨，下午是转晴了。
options.misconception: replaces each verb with 是, which reports three states and loses every change, so nothing appears to happen to the weather

options.text: 早上冷得很，后来下起了雨，下午又转晴了。
options.misconception: keeps the intensifier but drops the 起, which is what marks the rain as starting rather than as a fact being reported

options.text: 早上冷，后来下雨，后来又晴了，都是天气。
options.misconception: flattens three changes into a list with no intensifier, and the closing 都 is a complaint about a subject nobody asked about

questions.explanation: Three separate things are happening in this sentence and each needs its own device. Coldness to a high degree is expressed with the intensifier suffix 得, so 冷得很 is very cold, and 得 is the item learners most often drop. Starting is expressed with the resultative 起 together with the directional 来, so 下起雨来了 is the rain got under way rather than a report that there was rain. Returning to an earlier state is expressed with 又, and that is the job it does in 下午又转晴了, because the afternoon is a return to the clear weather the morning did not have. The distractors each lose one device and the losses are the ones a learner makes for understandable reasons. B is a substitution of the copula for every verb, which turns a description of change into a list of conditions and is the reason the sentence sounds like a weather report rather than like a person. C is the single most common omission in learner speech, because 下起了雨 is understandable and the 起 is easy to skip. D has neither the intensifier nor the change, and adds a generalisation at the end.
questions.hint: Ask which three devices are doing the work here, and then check each of them against the sentence.

questions.learningObjective: state a frequency accurately without overstating or contradicting it
questions.stem: A learner swims often but not every day, and he wants to say so accurately rather than impress. Which sentence is honest about the frequency?

options.text: 我经常去游泳，不过不是每天都去，一周大概两次。
我每天都游泳，一周七次，一次都没有落下。
options.misconception: overstates the claim by replacing a habit with a total, which is the mistake made when a learner wants to sound committed

options.text: 我有时候去游泳，很少去，一周也未必有一次。
options.misconception: puts two frequency adverbs in one sentence that point in opposite directions, so neither of them tells the listener anything

options.text: 我比较去游泳，有时候去，其实也不怎么去。
options.misconception: uses a word for degree where a word for frequency belongs, so the sentence makes a claim about how much swimming is and not about how often

questions.explanation: Saying how often something happens takes a word for frequency, and the honest version usually needs two of them: a general adverb and then a correction. 经常 supplies the general case, 不是每天都 knocks it back from every day, and 一周大概两次 replaces both with a figure. The sentence is longer than the claim strictly needs and that is the point, because a single adverb can only be as accurate as the person using it chooses to be. The distractors each fail in a way that is worth recognising in other people's speech as well as one's own. B is the exaggeration, and it is remarkably common in a job interview, where somebody is trying to signal a commitment they do not have and ends up claiming a perfection. C is the confusion that comes from having several adverbs available and not knowing which pair are compatible, and 未必 once has made the whole sentence unusable. D is the part of speech error, and 比较 is a marker of degree: it can say the swimming is quite hard, and it cannot say how many times it happens.
questions.hint: Ask which word carries frequency and which carries degree, and check that the two frequency statements agree.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: report past experience with the right aspect particle and no redundancy
questions.stem: A learner must say that she has been to Beijing once and has never been to Shanghai. Which pair says both without adding anything?

options.text: 我去过北京一次，上海我没去过。
我去过了北京一次，上海我没去过。
options.misconception: puts 了 after 过, which is redundant because 过 already marks an experience that is over and not repeated

options.text: 我去过北京，上海我没去过。
options.misconception: leaves out the count, so the claim of having been sounds unlimited rather than limited to one trip

options.text: 我去过北京一次，上海我也没去过。
options.misconception: adds 也 to the negative, which brings an unnamed companion into the statement that was only about the speaker

questions.explanation: 过 is the particle for experience: it says the event happened at some point in the past and the matter is closed, and it does its work on its own. Adding 了 after it adds nothing, because 了 marks a change of state that 过 has already marked, and the combination is one of the most reliable errors in learner speech precisely because the two particles are both common and both feel necessary. The count 一次 is a separate matter and it is doing real work, because without it the speaker has said she has been to Beijing and left a listener free to picture a great many trips. The negative needs no particle at all, since 没 already carries the tense, and it takes the form 我没去过. The last option adds 也, and that particle is for a comparison, so the sentence is now claiming something about other people that the speaker has not been asked about and may not know. Each distractor is a small addition, which is what makes the item diagnostic.
questions.hint: Ask what 过 already means, and then check whether the sentence adds a count, a companion, or a second particle.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: screen future-plan sentences for correct use of the prospective markers
questions.stem: A student wants to say he means to look for work this summer. Four of the five sentences below express that plan correctly. Which four?

options.text: 我打算今年夏天找工作。
我准备今年夏天找工作。
我想今年夏天找工作。
我要今年夏天找工作。
我将要今年夏天找工作。
options.misconception: treats 将 as a general marker of the future that goes with any time phrase, when it points at a reference time that has to be in the sentence

questions.explanation: Four of these say the same thing in four ways, and the reason all four work is worth stating, because it is the reason the fifth does not. 打算 and 准备 both name a plan that the speaker has made and is presenting as settled, and both are followed by the same shape, a time phrase and then a verb phrase, with no marker of tense required anywhere. 我要 names the intention more briefly and is equally available. 我想 is the weakest of the four and is still correct, because a wish and a plan are close enough in Chinese that a listener will hear the plan if the sentence is about what comes next. The fifth is the odd one out for a structural reason. 将 is not a general future marker in the way the other four function; it marks something future with respect to a reference point that the sentence itself supplies, which is why it is common with 以后 and with a stated change of circumstance. Put in front of a bare season and time phrase it has nothing to be relative to, and the sentence loses the sense of intention that all four of the others carry.
questions.hint: Ask which of the four markers needs a reference point in the sentence, and then check whether the sentence supplies one.

questions.learningObjective: build a hypothetical with the standard conditional and consequent markers
questions.stem: A learner wants to say that if he had more time he would go back and finish his degree, and the sentence has to be a hypothesis rather than a report. Which sentence pairs the two markers correctly?

options.text: 要是时间够，我就回去接着念书。
要是时间够，我才回去接着念书。
options.misconception: uses 才, which says the second half happens only when the condition fails, and so reverses the sense of the whole sentence

options.text: 要是时间够，我就已经回去念书了。
options.misconception: puts 已经 and 了 inside the consequence, so the sentence reports a completed state inside a supposition that has not happened

options.text: 要是时间够过，我就回去接着念书。
options.misconception: adds 过 to the condition, a particle that marks a completed past experience and has no place in an unreal supposition

questions.explanation: A Chinese hypothetical is a matched pair: 要是 opens the condition and 就 marks the consequence, and the two belong together closely enough that neither can be moved. The keyed sentence is the pattern, and it is used for suppositions the speaker believes are not true of the present. The distractors each bring in a particle that belongs somewhere else, and the interesting thing is that every one of them is a real particle doing a real job elsewhere. 才 is the opposite of the consequent, because it says the second half happens only if the first did not, so the sentence now means the opposite of what the learner meant. 已经 and 了 together describe a finished state, which is exactly the wrong tense for a supposition; a hypothesis has no result yet, so a result inside it is a contradiction. 过 is the hardest one to see, because it looks like a softener, but it reports that something was done and finished at some past time, and a supposition is not that. The rule worth keeping is short: in a hypothesis the consequence carries nothing but 就.
questions.hint: Ask which particle marks the consequence in a hypothesis, and then check what each of the other three would assert.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A register claim a particle contradicts
questions.learningObjective: find the particle that contradicts a claim of formality and repair it
questions.stem: A learner writes to a manager and claims the message is entirely formal: 您好，我想跟您商量一下这件事，麻烦您了，好吧？ Explain exactly what gives that claim away, say what each other item in the sentence is doing, and rewrite the ending so the register is consistent.

answer.exemplar: The claim fails on the last two characters, and it is worth being able to say why, because 好吧 is the item a learner is most confident about. It is made of two particles that each work, separately and for different reasons. 吧 proposes, or softens, and it carries the sense of a suggestion offered to somebody who is free to decline. 了 marks that a situation has come to an end. Together 好吧 asks the manager to ratify something the writer has already decided, and a manager hears it as a familiar form, the register of a colleague or a flatmate. Everything before it is right, and that is what makes the item worth setting: 您好 is the respectful greeting, 我想 is a soft opener rather than a demand, 跟您商量 makes the request a negotiation, 麻烦您了 is the standard way of acknowledging the trouble, and 您 is the pronoun that carries the formality throughout. So the sentence is not under-informed about register; it is a good formal sentence with a casual ending attached, and the diagnosis has to be that precise, because telling a learner the whole message is too casual sends them looking for a different problem that is not there. The repair is a rewrite of the tail and nothing else. Dropping the two characters gives 您好，我想跟您商量一下这件事，麻烦您了，谢谢。, which closes the request with thanks and keeps every other item intact. Another good repair is to keep 吧 and remove the 了, so the request reads as a genuine proposal that the manager can accept or decline, and a learner who can choose between those two repairs understands that register is a property of the whole sentence and not a matter of picking the politest word.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked as correct for isolating the fault to the final particle pair, for saying what each of the other four items is doing, and for deriving a repair from the diagnosis rather than replacing the whole sentence. A response that says only the tone is too casual has not done the work, and a response that rewrites the greeting has diagnosed the wrong clause.
questions.hint: Ask which two characters at the end of the sentence do work no other item in the message does, and what the two of them do together.

questions.topic: A complaint and its first level
questions.learningObjective: raise a complaint at the level where it can still be solved
questions.stem: A customer in a restaurant has been served the wrong dish and wants it dealt with without a scene and without being given a lecture. Which complaint is right for a first approach?

options.text: 不好意思，我点的是这个，不是那个，麻烦您帮我换一下。
这也搞错了？你们店里到底还能不能做事？

questions.learningObjective: escalate a repeated request without losing politeness at any step
questions.stem: A guest has asked three times for water at a busy restaurant and has not been answered. Which sequence escalates each time, keeps the politeness, and adds something new at every step?

麻烦给杯水。 / 麻烦给杯水。 / 水！快点，谢谢。
options.misconception: repeats the same request twice with no new information, and turns the third attempt into an order to an individual employee

options.text: 给我倒杯水。 / 你怎么回事，水还没来？ / 我等了半个小时了，这店今天真是没道理。
options.misconception: starts with a bare command and ends by criticising the restaurant, so there is no politeness left by the time it is most needed

The third names the actual situation, that the water has still not arrived, and then asks somebody to look at it, which is a request the waiter can act on in front of a manager. Firmness has come from specificity rather than from volume. The other three are the ways this goes wrong. C is the version a learner produces under stress, and the failure is at the front: a bare 给我 to a stranger removes every politeness before the first attempt, so the later complaints have no goodwill left to spend. D is the failure of mistaking softening for escalation, and three requests stacked on polite particles is a longer message that is no stronger.

喂，请问是星海公司吗？ / 我是上个月来过的林涛。 / 好的，谢谢您，再见。 / 我想问上个月那份订单现在到哪儿了。

questions.explanation: The sequence in the first option is the one a Chinese phone call follows, and the reason is that each turn supplies the person answering with the one thing they need before the next turn can mean anything. 喂 gets attention from somebody who does not yet know who has called. 请问是星海公司吗 checks that the call reached the right organisation, and until that is answered the speaker has no idea whether to discuss an order. questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Repairing the register of an apology
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a register fault in an apology and rewrite it for a second audience
questions.stem: Stage one: a learner wrote one apology and sent it to two people, a manager and a close friend, in the form 真的很抱歉，我那天临时有事，没能去。 Say precisely why one sentence cannot do both jobs. Stage two: produce the two sentences, and say what each one had to give up to reach the right register.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. The sentence is not wrong; it is uniformly mid-register, and that is the diagnosis. 真的很抱歉 is at the level of careful speech, which is what a manager should receive and more than a friend needs. 那天临时有事 as an explanation is thin: it gives a category and no content, and a manager is being asked to accept an excuse of the kind a learner offers when the truth is unavailable, while a friend would have accepted a single word. 没能去 is written in a way that works for both audiences, so the sentence has no part that is friendly, and it has no part that is formal beyond the apology itself. One sentence cannot do both jobs because register is carried by several items at once, not by one, and each audience needs a different setting of all of them. The deeper point for a learner is that the failure is not politeness. Both sentences are polite; one is polite to the wrong distance. Stage two. The manager's version keeps the apology at its careful level, names a reason a reader can accept as concrete rather than as a category, and adds an acknowledgement of the trouble caused: 真的很抱歉，那天下班以后突然发烧，去了医院，所以没能去开会，是我准备得不够。 The clause about preparation is what earns the sentence its formality, because it locates the fault in the writer. The friend's version drops every one of those items and keeps only what a friend needs: 抱歉，那天我病了，没能去，下次补上。 The intensifier is gone, the reason is a single word, the sentence is short, and the promise to make it up is added instead of the apology for being at fault. What each version gives up is worth stating, because that is the discipline: the manager's version gives up ease, since it is longer and heavier than a friendship requires, and the friend's version gives up standing, since a sentence that short with a writer who has just missed something sounds like a person who does not think it was a problem.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked as correct for diagnosing the fault as even mid-register rather than as impolite, for identifying the thin explanation as the part that fails for both audiences, and for naming what each rewritten sentence gives up rather than only what it gains. A rewrite that simply makes the manager version longer is the failure this item is set against.
questions.hint: Ask which items in the one sentence carry register, and which part of it would neither audience be satisfied with.

questions.topic: Resultant state against an action in progress
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a state left by a change from an action at its moment

The fourth is register, and it is the one that does the least and the one learners attempt first. questions.topic: 麻烦 and 不好意思
questions.learningObjective: explain the difference between two softening words to a learner
questions.stem: A learner knows 麻烦 and 不好意思 and uses them interchangeably. Explain what each one acknowledges, why they cannot do each other's job, and give a situation in which only one of them works.

answer.exemplar: The difference is what each one puts on the table. 麻烦 acknowledges that the act being asked for will cost the other person something, and it names the other person as the one incurring the cost, which is why it needs a pronoun and why 麻烦您 is the complete phrase. It is for trouble: work, waiting, an interruption to something the other person was in the middle of. 不好意思 is an apology for the act of speaking at all, and it takes the weight off the moment rather than off the task, which is why it is the right word for interrupting, for arriving late, for having said something clumsy. That is why they cannot substitute. A learner who says 不好意思我要用您的车 has apologised for the fact of speaking and has still announced a requirement, and the request has not been made askable. A learner who says 麻烦我迟到了 has named their own lateness as trouble for themselves, which is not what the sentence means and not what the listener needs. The situations divide cleanly. A manager is in a meeting and a learner needs thirty seconds: 不好意思 is the right word, because the cost being acknowledged is the interruption, and 麻烦 would be too heavy for thirty seconds. A colleague has been asked to redo a report and the request is genuinely inconvenient: 麻烦 is the right word, because the cost is the work, and an 不好意思 there would apologise for asking without ever asking. A learner who has internalised this will also stop searching for a third synonym, and will notice that 请 sits in a different family again, being a marker of the request itself rather than a comment on its cost.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked as correct for naming the cost each word acknowledges, for giving one situation for each where only that word works, and for keeping 请 in a separate family rather than treating it as a third interchangeable softener. A response that says 麻烦 is more formal than 不好意思 is right about the ranking and wrong about the reason, and the reason is what transfers.
questions.hint: Ask what cost each word is acknowledging, and then find a situation where the other one is needed.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Why a politeness marker is not enough
questions.learningObjective: teach a learner why a politeness word does not by itself make a sentence polite
questions.stem: A learner is convinced that adding 请 to any request makes it polite and has written 请你马上把钱还给我 to somebody older than her. Explain what the sentence actually does in Chinese, what politeness in this language is attached to instead, and what the learner should check in any sentence she thinks is polite.

answer.exemplar: The sentence is not merely impolite, and the distinction matters for teaching. It is well-formed, it is unambiguous, and it is a demand with a deadline attached, issued by a younger person to an older one, using the pronoun that asserts equality. 请 at the front is a marker that the act is a request rather than a statement, and it is doing its job exactly as designed: the sentence is a request. A reader who believed that 请 settles the matter of tone has misread the function of the word, because 请 belongs to the family of markers and none of them in that family carries politeness on its own. In this language politeness is attached to things a person is rather than to things a sentence contains. The relation is carried by the pronoun, since 您 and 你 are not two shades of politeness but two different relationships, and the one chosen here is the one that cannot be used towards an elder. The relative rank of the two speakers is carried the same way. The size of what is being asked of the other person is carried by whether there is a way to refuse, and a 马上 leaves none. And the cost to the other person is carried by whether the request acknowledges one, which this sentence does not. So the check to teach is a question with four parts: which pronoun, which relative rank, can the reader refuse, and has the cost been named. A sentence can pass none of these and still contain 请, and it will still be understood as a demand, because the listener is reading the pronoun and the rank and not the marker. The productive consequence for the learner is that when a sentence of hers sounds wrong and she cannot see why, the answer will be in those four things and not in the choice between politeness words.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked as correct for insisting that the sentence is a well-formed request rather than a grammatical failure, for locating politeness on the relation rather than on a marker, and for giving a four-part check the learner can apply to her own sentences. A response that only says the pronoun is wrong identifies one of the four and stops short of the method.
questions.hint: Ask which pronoun is used, whether the reader can refuse, and whether the cost to the reader has been named anywhere.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A polite message that pushes work back
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a courteous message whose effect is to transfer the work
questions.stem: Stage one: a learner writes 麻烦您了，明天记得把材料发给我, to a colleague who has asked for help. Diagnose what the sentence does to the balance of work between them. Stage two: rewrite it so the balance is right, and say which of your changes actually moved the balance rather than only the tone.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. The sentence is courteous and it is a transfer. 麻烦您了 announces trouble and thanks for it in one breath, and 记得 is the item that does the work: it presents the sending as something the other person will recall rather than as something being arranged, and it makes an omission into a fault. Combined with a deadline given as a fact, the sentence asks a favour and then attaches a condition, and the condition is the part that will be remembered. The net effect is that the learner names the work as somebody else's and reserves the right to be upset about the timing, so the politeness is real and the request is not equal. A useful test for the learner is to count who has to do something on account of this message. If the answer is only the other person, the message is a demand wearing the grammar of a favour. Stage two. The rewrite has to do two separate things, and they should be kept separate because only one of them works. The first is to take the work back: the learner states what they will do, and when, so that the reader is not holding a task. The second is to let the deadline be a preference, which is done by moving it out of an assertion and into a request with a question ending, so that the other person can answer no. A candidate rewrite is something in the shape of 这件事本来是我这边要做的，明天我早点发给你，要是来得及就太好了；实在赶不上你跟我说一声，我们换个时间。 That sentence has moved the work, made refusal safe, and kept the urgency, and it has done all three without becoming long. Which change did the balance: the first clause, because it takes the task back and makes the other person's action optional. Everything else in the rewrite is tone, and tone was never the defect. A learner who fixes only the tone will produce a softer demand and will not notice that the demand is still there, which is the specific failure this item is set to catch.

questions.explanation: The pairing tests a diagnosis and a repair. The exemplar is marked as correct for identifying 记得 as the item that converts an arrangement into an omission, for giving a test based on who has to do the work, and for saying which of its own changes moved the balance and which were only tone.
questions.hint: Ask who has to do something on account of the message, and then ask whether the reader could say no to the deadline without giving an excuse.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: convert a refusal between registers and say what each version gives up
questions.stem: Stage one: a learner wants to refuse an invitation to a manager in a way that will not close a door. Say what has to be false in the sentence for the refusal to land correctly, and why a bare no does that job badly. Stage two: write the refusal, and say what you gave up in order to keep the relationship available.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. Two things have to be true at once, and the difficulty of this refusal is that they pull against each other. The refusal has to be definite, because a refusal that could be read as a maybe leaves the other person waiting and is worse than a no. And it has to be open, because a refusal that carries no other door is a refusal with a cost attached to it. A bare no fails on the second count rather than the first, and it fails because in Chinese, as in most languages, a very short refusal is read as a statement about the person rather than about the fact. What the refusal cannot contain is an apology for needing the time, because apologising for a constraint you did not choose hands the other person a reason to think you would come if pressed, and the invitation will be made again. It also cannot contain a promise to do it another time, because a promise with no date is a way of refusing that is easier to feel and harder to act on. Stage two. The shape that works puts the reason first, in the passive, so that the constraint is the world rather than the speaker, then the refusal, and then something that leaves a future open without promising anything. A candidate is in the shape of 下个月我这边正好有一个项目要收尾，实在走不开，所以这次我就不去了；等这个项目结束以后，您再叫我我一定来。 Three things are worth naming about it. The reason is given before the refusal, which is the Chinese order and which is why a listener is not treated as an obstacle to the news. The reason is impersonal, so the speaker is not a person who would rather be elsewhere. And the last clause opens a door without a date, which is the compromise the whole sentence is built around, since a dated promise is a commitment and an undated one is a courtesy. What was given up is real and should not be pretended away: the speaker has declined warmly and therefore has not created the impression of having been keen, which is a genuine loss and a price some speakers will decide is too high.

questions.explanation: The pairing tests a diagnosis and a production. The exemplar is marked as correct for naming the two conditions that must hold at once, for identifying the apologetic reason and the dateless promise as the two traps, and for stating what the rewrite costs rather than only what it gains.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence could be read as a maybe, whether it apologises for a constraint it did not choose, and whether it promises a date.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: state a boundary as a limit rather than as an apology
questions.stem: A learner has to say that a plan is possible but only in a reduced form, and the sentence must not apologise for the limit itself. Which sentence does that?

options.text: 这个可以做，不过只能先做一半，剩下的要下周才能补上。
实在对不起，我只能先做一半，剩下的下周补，很抱歉。
options.misconception: apologises twice for a limit rather than stating it, which makes a constraint sound like a fault the speaker committed

options.text: 这个可以一半，剩下的一半我就不管了，你们自己想办法。
options.misconception: hands the remainder back without any reason, so the listener is left with a gap and no information

options.text: 这个一半吧，剩下一半的话我也没办法，我很对不起你们。
options.misconception: marks the limit with a suggestion particle and then apologises for it, so the sentence both softens the plan and takes responsibility for it

questions.explanation: A limit is a fact about capacity and does not need an apology, and the wording that keeps it a fact is the one that marks the restriction as a maximum. 只能 says that this is the ceiling, which is a statement about what is available rather than about what the speaker feels about the request, and 只 does most of that work on its own. The keyed sentence pairs it with a clear division, half now and the rest after a named time, so the listener knows both how much is coming and when the rest arrives. The distractors each add something the sentence should not carry. B apologises twice, and twice is the point: an apology for a capacity limit reframes a constraint as a failure, and a listener who has heard an apology will often lower the expectation further, which defeats the speaker. C gives the limit and then abandons the remainder, so the work is now nobody's, and that is the outcome a speaker is trying to avoid. D marks the limit with 吧, which turns it into a suggestion the other person may overrule, and then apologises for having suggested it.
questions.hint: Ask whether the sentence apologises for the limit, and whether the listener learns when the rest will come.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the verb that means to pass on what somebody else said
questions.stem: A learner is asked to tell a colleague what their manager said in a meeting the learner attended. Which sentence does the job without claiming to have been the one who decided it?

options.text: 王经理说，让你这个星期把表格改完交给他。
我要你把这个星期把表格改完交给我。
options.misconception: changes the subject of the original order and the person who is to receive the result, so the relay reports something nobody said

options.text: 王经理大概的意思是，表格这个星期最好改完。
options.misconception: softens the manager's instruction into a preference and drops the part about who receives the table, so the colleague hears an option

options.text: 王经理说了，不过我也没太听清，好像是要改表格。
options.misconception: acknowledges that the relay is unreliable and then reports it anyway, which leaves the colleague with a task and no confidence

questions.explanation: Relaying somebody else's words has a marker and the marker is the subject position. Naming the person who said it keeps the instruction theirs, and it lets the speaker pass on the content without appearing to add anything of their own, which is the whole purpose of the exercise when the manager is senior. The content itself is best kept in its original directive shape, because a message that has been softened on the way is a message that has been changed, and the colleague will act on the version they were given. The distractors each lose that boundary. B is the change of speaker that learners make when they do not realise the pronoun in a relayed message is still the original speaker's, and it is a serious error, because the colleague now believes the learner has authority they do not have. C softens an instruction into a suggestion and drops the recipient, and a colleague who hears it will treat the week as optional. D is the honest uncertainty, and it is the one that still causes harm, since the task is passed on with no idea how firm it is, and the colleague cannot check anything.
questions.hint: Ask who said the sentence, whether the directive has survived the journey, and who is to receive the result.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Saying something versus speaking about something
questions.learningObjective: separate the verb for speaking from the verb for speaking about
questions.stem: A learner has to write that a person raised a difficult subject with the manager, and has three verbs to choose from. Which sentence uses the right one?

options.text: 她跟经理谈过这件事，经理没有生气。
她说这件事说了三遍，经理没有生气。
options.misconception: uses the verb for producing words rather than the verb for raising a matter, so the sentence reports utterance and not a discussion

options.text: 她跟经理聊了这事，聊了整整一个下午，经理没有生气。
options.misconception: uses the verb for casual conversation and adds a duration, so the subject sounds trivial rather than difficult

options.text: 她跟经理说这件事要小心点，经理没有生气。
options.misconception: reports the learner reporting something else, and adds a warning the manager never gave

questions.explanation: Chinese has a small set of verbs for speaking and they are not interchangeable, and the difference between them is a difference about what was done rather than about how. 谈 is raising a matter with somebody, which is what a report needs, and the particle 过 is doing real work in the keyed sentence because it marks the discussion as something that has happened and is now over, so a listener can tell a past conversation from a present one. 说 is the general verb for producing words, and a sentence built on it can only report that words were uttered, not that anything was settled, which is why B describes talking rather than raising a subject. 聊 belongs to informal conversation and carries a lightness that fights the word 难 in the stem, and the duration in C makes it worse. The other failure in the same family is worth naming: a learner sometimes reaches for 说 and then supplies a direct quote, which switches the sentence from a report of a discussion to a report of something said, and D is that error with an invented warning in it.
questions.hint: Ask whether the verb reports words that were produced or a matter that was raised, and check the particle for a past event.
